**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                       Date Issued: 21 February 2011</mark>** 



ICSG Surveys on Regulatory Developments Affecting Copper: 2008, 2009 and 2010 Editions 

The International Copper Study Group has released for sale the results of its regulatory developments surveys carried out in 2008, 2009 and 2010. The reports present a detailed review of the dynamics of the regulations in the non‐ferrous metals industry affecting copper in various jurisdictions worldwide. 

**Contents of ICSG Survey of Regulations 2010.** The 2010 edition covers 50 new regulations implemented or discussed in 2009‐2010. In relation to China requests for import tax rebates on raw materials such as copper scrap are considered, together with possible import duties on energy and the tax exemptions on other copper commodities such as blister which aim to increase import flow. Outside China the proposed mining tax in Australia and in Chile the earthquake‐related royalty are examined. In Brazil the option to raise mining taxes is being debated, and the limit of mining licenses lifetime impact on competitiveness. In the 2010 edition we identified positive developments for copper trade and investment in the <mark>Free Trade Agreement between Peru and China, the efforts of</mark> India to improve electronic waste disposal, and the use of mining concession auction procedures in Ecuador. The United States EPA effort to monitor greenhouse emissions are discussed. UNEP’s first intergovernmental session on mercury allowed us to examine the positions of different nations on a proposed global ban of mercury. The United Nations’ Globally Harmonised System 2010 deadline is discussed together with advances to comply with the European REACH Regulation and the advances for an EU End of Waste regulation for copper and alloy scrap. 

**Contents of ICSG Survey of Regulations 2009.** The report summarizes China’s stimulus package and the copper‐related objectives of China’s Non Ferrous Metals Plan 2009‐2011. A summary of Chinese trade and metal recycling regulations that affected global copper markets is included. A summary of changes in mining legislations around the world in 2008/2009 is discussed. Air quality regulation updates in Canada affecting copper smelters are presented. The challenge for the copper industry of a United States mercury trade ban and the proposed UNEP Global Mercury Ban is discussed. European regulatory trends are summarized, including the evolution of the EU Directive on Water Quality, the implementation and challenges of REACH registration for copper slag and the 13 copper intermediates, and a summary of the WEEE Directive changes proposed by EU recyclers and the copper‐related EC End of Waste proposal. 

**Contents of ICSG Survey of Regulations 2008.** The report identifies international agreements related to climate change and their impacts on energy generation and compliance costs. Advances in the design of EU energy and climate chan

ge regulations, the implementation of chemical control legislation (REACH) and changes in the EU Drinking Water Directive are included. The United States Senate Bill 2006 restricting activities of scrap metal traders is summarized. For China, the 2008 Survey includes the decree raising the selling price of electricity, coke coal and aluminum export tariffs in China, strengthened controls on inflows of foreign exchange, the import prohibition of copper related wastes, and the approved recycling law effective in 2009. Indonesia’s new mining legislation is summarized, and mining law developments in Kazakhstan and Zambia are considered. # **International Copper Study Group Order Form** Prices are quoted in Euros.
